_comment: TARGET-tier). One per crustify invocation target. It names the campaign's
objective and its two file sets, plus a target-local refinement of what is
out of scope. Values below illustrate a run scoped to ssl/statem inside an
openssl checkout; substitute for other projects.
_comment_layout: All crustify artifacts live under a single `crustify/` directory at the
repository root (which also marks the root). REPO-ROOT-tier artifacts are
TARGET-tier artifacts live under crustify/targets/<target>/ and are
invocation-scoped: this scope-config.json, the derived scope.json, and
The repo root and the target id are CLI positionals
under `crustify/targets/<target>/` records the target. Neither is
restated here: a second copy can only drift from the invocation.
_comment_campaign_objective: What this campaign is FOR - `port` or `wrap`. REQUIRED, with no default.
It is the ONLY thing that decides how the two file sets below are read:
`port`  reimplement the target in Rust. `impl_files` + `api_headers`
together seed scope.json's `targeted` section, on
DEFINITION-anchored membership: an entity is targeted iff its
BODY lives in a named file (or, having no body, all its
declarations do). Everything those entities REACH but that is
not named is derived automatically into the sibling `imported`
section.
`wrap`  expose the target's public API from Rust, owning none of it.
The `targeted` section composes EMPTY and `imported` is seeded
off `api_headers` directly, on DECLARATION-site membership -
the right test for a public header, whose declared bodies live
in files this campaign does not own. `impl_files` is not read.
This is how you wrap a whole library.
Everything follows from that one word, with no per-item flag: a struct
DEFINED in a named file keeps its full field layout (its fields are the
API), one merely forward-declared stays an opaque handle; a targeted symbol
orders on its body's callees, an imported one only on its signature. So
`--transitive` over an opaque type pulls the type and nothing else.
This is NOT the per-wave `translate --objective`, which is the verb handed
to one agent over one selection (wrap | port | review | raw). This says
what the whole campaign is aimed at, and it shapes the scope; that says
what one agent does with a slice of it. Narrowing to an API SURFACE is a
SELECTION concern (`translate --file include/openssl/ssl.h`), not either.
`crustify-oracle <root> <target> query dag --full` reads a `wrap`
campaign's graph as if it were `port` - bodies walked, all fields kept -
without editing this file.
Ownership analysis is unaffected either way: ptr_args/ptr_ret come from the
T2 tables, which cover the whole database regardless of scope.
_comment_files: The campaign's two file sets. BOTH are authored whatever the objective -
they describe the library, not the campaign - and both are
repo-root-relative and always explicit; there is no implicit directory
walk. Entries are either:
* a FILE      - `include/internal/statem.h`
* a DIRECTORY, written with a trailing slash - `ssl/` - which expands
to every source/header file beneath it
`out_of_scope.paths` applies to whatever a directory entry expands to.
Naming a file the build never compiled is harmless: scope.json is anchored
on the T1 tables, so uncompiled candidates simply drop out.
`impl_files`   the sources - and the private headers - that IMPLEMENT
the library. Name the implementations AND the internal
headers that DEFINE the types: a header outside the
target tree is never discovered on its own, and a
header-only list would drop every function it merely
declares.
`api_headers`  the headers that PUBLISH the API (`include/openssl/`,
`include/libxml/`), not its sources. On a `wrap`
campaign these are the seed and nothing else is read; on
a `port` campaign they join `impl_files`, because the
structs the ported code implements are declared there.
_comment_out_of_scope: Target-local refinement of what crustify must NOT analyze. `paths` lists
repo-root-relative paths (directories with trailing `/` recurse; entries
without are exact-file matches) that the composer skips while expanding
`impl_files` / `api_headers`, even when a directory entry there covers
them. Project-wide exclusions (e.g. `apps/`, `fuzz/`) are implicit via not
being named at all - list them here only if a directory entry would
otherwise pull them in. `features` lists macro feature names (typically
`OPENSSL_NO_<FEATURE>` or equivalent) the user wants treated as
disabled. NOTE: like `build.json`'s `features` block, this list is
currently DOCUMENTATION ONLY - no composer reads it. Dead code is
filtered implicitly instead: scope.json is anchored on the T1 tables, so
a body elided by a disabled feature contributes no entities and its file
